relations.myth: Female Odù bears the principal signs
relations.note: Female Odù bears or encompasses the principal Odù and governs their mystery.
Some lineages make Ọ̀rúnmìlà the father of the principal Odù.

relations.myth: Ọ̀rúnmìlà interprets and transmits Ifá
relations.note: Ọ̀rúnmìlà serves as custodian and interpreter through whom the signs speak.

relations.myth: Odù gives Ifá to Ọ̀rúnmìlà
relations.note: Female Odù teaches or gives Ọ̀rúnmìlà the knowledge and means of divination.

relations.myth: Odù marries Ọ̀rúnmìlà and grants access
relations.note: In lineage variants, female Odù marries Ọ̀rúnmìlà and conditionally transfers her sacred authority.

relations.myth: Olódùmarè authorizes cosmic knowledge
relations.note: Olódùmarè authorizes the wisdom and allotted destiny disclosed through the Odù.

relations.myth: Èṣù conveys sacrifices and enforces compliance
relations.note: Èṣù mediates the Odù’s prescriptions, carries offerings, tests compliance, and affects results.

relations.myth: Ẹ̀là voices the efficacy of Ifá
relations.note: Ẹ̀là is invoked as Ifá’s saving voice or manifestation, though its ontology varies.

relations.myth: Odù disclose and repair personal destiny
relations.note: The Odù reveal a client’s Orí and prescribe actions to repair its condition.

relations.myth: Divination before creation and human formation
relations.note: Ọbàtálá receives divination before creation; compliance or refusal changes the outcome.

relations.myth: Odùduwà consults Ifá before descent or kingship
relations.note: Odùduwà consults the Odù concerning descent, earth-making, settlement, or royal authority.

relations.myth: Ògún consults before warfare or entering earth
relations.note: The Odù advise Ògún about war, roads, iron, or descent and prescribe sacrifice.

relations.myth: Ògún refuses the prescribed sacrifice
relations.note: In some verses, Ògún suffers adverse consequences after refusing the Odù’s sacrifice.

relations.myth: Ṣàngó consults during royal crisis
relations.note: Ṣàngó consults the Odù about kingship, enemies, thunder, or personal crisis.

relations.myth: Male Òrìṣà fail until recognizing Ọ̀ṣun
relations.note: A verse recounts failed collective projects until Ọ̀ṣun’s indispensable agency is acknowledged.

relations.myth: Ajé consults Ifá for enduring prosperity
relations.note: The Odù direct wealth through sacrifices and good character necessary to retain prosperity.

relations.myth: Death is negotiated through an Odù
relations.note: Odù prescriptions negotiate, delay, or accept death, with outcomes differing among narratives.
The Odù disclose obligations to ancestral powers and prescribe the required rites.

relations.myth: Powerful mothers are appeased or opposed
relations.note: Depending on the verse, the Odù prescribe appeasing, respecting, or opposing the powerful mothers.

relations.myth: Yemọja receives verse-specific divination
relations.note: Yemọja appears in particular verses as client, beneficiary, rival, diviner, or sacrificial recipient.

relations.myth: Ifá descends and gains early transmitters
relations.note: Akódá becomes an early disciple and authoritative transmitter of the Odù corpus.

relations.myth: Ifá descends and gains early transmitters
relations.note: Aṣedá becomes an early disciple and authoritative transmitter of the Odù corpus.
